name: BGF MDI 320/14.4/9.6 μg
note: THARROS (NCT06283966), the cardiopulmonary outcomes trial in COPD, names its arm 'BGF MDI 320/14.4/9.6 μg: Budesonide, glycopyrronium, and formoterol fumarate pressurized inhalation suspension' (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, read 2026-10-28). That is Breztri's COPD dose: the label (DailyMed setid 715433dc-cb2b-43ea-b6df-c5b4177adc6c) gives 2 inhalations twice daily of 160 mcg budesonide, 9 mcg glycopyrrolate 'equivalent to 7.2 ... mcg of glycopyrronium' and 4.8 mcg formoterol fumarate, so 320/14.4/9.6 per dose. AstraZeneca's FY2025 20-F (0001104659-26-019130) lists 'Breztri / Trixeo THARROS ... cardiopulmonary outcomes trial in COPD'. data/asset_alias_map.csv already folds 'BGF MDI' into Breztri; the registry spelled this arm with its strength, so it arrived as a row of its own. Breztri is modelled (data/assumptions/azn_breztri.csv). COPD is Breztri's approved disease, so a layer for this readout is base_pool_overlap_pct 1.0; on this copy asset 786 carries only an Asthma indication row, so the readout needs a COPD row to land on

name: Budesonide/Albuterol metered dose inhaler, MDI
note: BAIYUN (NCT06471257, asthma, China) names the intervention 'Budesonide/Albuterol metered dose inhaler, MDI' with other name PT027 against 'Albuterol sulfate metered dose inhaler, MDI' (PT007). Airsupra is albuterol and budesonide in a metered dose inhaler (DailyMed setid e60aa9f9-5139-44df-b886-ebddc3c7eb13: 'AIRSUPRA (ALBUTEROL SULFATE AND BUDESONIDE) AEROSOL, METERED', 180 mcg/160 mcg as 2 actuations of 90/80) and is modelled (data/assumptions/azn_airsupra.csv). data/asset_alias_map.csv already maps 'BDA MDI' to Airsupra. Asthma is Airsupra's approved US indication and BAIYUN enrols Chinese adults, so the readout is a China registration, not a new US population

name: NCT04379596
note: DESTINY-Gastric03, 'Ph1b/2 Study of the Safety and Efficacy of T-DXd Combinations in Advanced HER2-expressing Gastric Cancer': every arm is trastuzumab deruxtecan (other names 'DS-8201a, Enhertu') alone or with a partner, and capecitabine, 5-FU, oxaliplatin, cisplatin, durvalumab, pembrolizumab, volrustomig and rilvegostomig are the partners (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, read 2026-10-28). The registry's first named intervention put the study on a 'Capecitabine' row, and the catalyst (id 301) carries asset_id 516, Imfinzi, while its indication row is Capecitabine's Stomach Neoplasms; neither is the drug under test. Enhertu is modelled (data/assumptions/azn_enhertu.csv); on this copy its asset (967) has no Stomach Neoplasms row, so the readout needs one. Enhertu is approved in previously treated HER2-positive gastric cancer, and this study tests first-line combinations

name: Dato-DXd
note: the registry names the drug 'Dato-DXd' with other name 'Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd, DS-1062a)' (NCT06103864 TROPION-Breast05, NCT05629585 TROPION-Breast03; NCT06417814 TROPION-Lung15 gives 'DS-1062a'), and Datroway is datopotamab deruxtecan-dlnk, the asset that absorbed BLA761464 and BLA761394. The Datroway model is written (azn_datroway.csv) and held in work/indication_backfill/held/HELD.md for its uncapped growth row, so these four readouts price once it is released, not through a second model

name: Lenbelintide
note: SELENE 3 (NCT07776509) names the intervention 'Lenbelintide' with other name AZD6234, and its title reads 'A Study to Evaluate Effect of AZD6234 as an Adjunct to Incretin-based Therapies'. data/assumptions/azn_azd6234.csv models AZD6234 in obesity and cites NCT07776509 among its own Phase 3 trials; the other AZD6234 studies (NCT07784725, NCT07784270) already sit on the AZD6234 row (asset 1690)

name: BMS-986489 (Atigotatug+Nivolumab)
note: TIGOS (NCT06646276) names the drug 'BMS-986489 (Atigotatug+Nivolumab)', and data/assumptions/bmy_bms_986489.csv models exactly that fixed-dose combination on exactly that trial. FLAG: no asset on this copy is named 'BMS-986489', so programme_alias.load_curated cannot resolve this target and assumptions.load_seeds skips every row of bmy_bms_986489.csv (asset 1934 carries 0 assumption rows on r7_post). The seed loads only once its brand column or the asset's name match; that edit is outside this group's files

name: ABP 938 8 mg
note: Amgen calls the 8 mg programme by Pavblu's development code: 'A randomized, double-blind, comparative clinical study of ABP 938 (8 mg) compared with EYLEA HD (aflibercept) was initiated' (Q2 2026 earnings release, 8-K 0000318154-26-000124), and Pavblu is that code: 'the FDA approved PAVBLU (aflibercept-ayyh) (ABP 938), a biosimilar candidate to EYLEA' (Q3 2024 earnings release, 8-K 0000318154-24-000042), BLA761298. NCT07614776 compares ABP 938 8 mg with Eylea HD in wet AMD. Pavblu itself has no model (asset 573, 0 assumption rows) though Amgen reports it ($287mm in Q2 2026, same release). The 8 mg readout reaches Eylea HD's patients, which Pavblu's revenue does not contain, so it is a real layer once Pavblu has a forecast; its start cannot yet be dated, because the book holds Eylea HD's US exclusivity as Regeneron's HD-only formulation patent 11,103,552 to 2039-05-15 (data/disclosed_loe.csv) and no Amgen filing, suit or settlement on the 8 mg product is on file

name: NCT07871513
note: 'A Study to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of Co-Reconstituted TrenibotulinumtoxinE and OnabotulinumtoxinA in Adult Participants With Moderate to Severe Upper Facial Lines': onabotulinumtoxinA is Botox (BLA103000), one of the two toxins in the syringe and the active comparator arm. Upper facial lines are already on Botox Cosmetic's US label (DailyMed setid 485d9b71-6881-42c5-a620-a4360c7192ab: glabellar, lateral canthal and forehead lines), and abbv_botox.csv's base revenue includes Botox Cosmetic ($2,602mm of $6,371mm, FY2025 10-K 0001551152-26-000008), so the readout is a line extension inside revenue the book already holds: a layer is base_pool_overlap_pct 1.0. TrenibotulinumtoxinE alone (Boey) received a US complete response letter on manufacturing in April 2026 and EC approval in July 2026 (10-Q 0001551152-26-000026); no asset in the book carries it
